Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>

Subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps — Finovate Bank

Hi Tom & Priya,

Great to chat this morning — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: reduce latency and per-call cost for customer support LLM features (chat summarization + routing).
- Targeted throughput: ~1500 QPS at peak for smaller prompt sizes.
- Success metrics: 40% reduction in per-message cost, sub-200ms p50 inference latency for the primary flow.

Open questions we discussed (please confirm):
1) Economic buyer: who ultimately signs approvals for a committed capacity purchase? (Tom/you mentioned finance involvement)
2) Procurement/security checklist: you mentioned a standard procurement packet — can you share the contact or the specific docs they need (SOC 2, DPA, vendor security questionnaire)?
3) Timeline: preferred procurement/PO window and any blackout dates for quarter-end?

Attachments: I attached a short ROI model and an initial SOW draft that outlines a phased Dedicated deployment + rollout milestones.
- Finovate_ROI_model_v3.xlsx (assumptions slide + TCO comparison)
- Redwood_SOW_draft.docx (scope, milestones, pricing bands)

Proposed next steps:
- Priya, would you be our internal champion for the technical + ops stakeholders?
- Tom, can you confirm the economic buyer (name + best intro)? If it’s finance, an intro to Lydia Chen (CFO) would be ideal.
- If procurement needs a point-of-contact, please loop them in and we’ll send the security brief and pricing spreadsheet.
- Assuming yes, suggested next meeting: stakeholder mapping workshop (30–45m) — options: Tue 3/2 10–10:45am PT or Wed 3/3 2–2:45pm PT.

Happy to adjust — thanks again and looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference | (415) 555-0124

Team — FYI and request. Thread below with Finovate. They confirmed Priya as champion and Lydia Chen (CFO) as economic buyer. Procurement asked for security docs and pricing.

What I need from you for Monday EOD (3/2):
- Lukas: a 1-page security brief (SOC 2 scope, data handling, audit logs, retention options) that we can share with procurement. Keep it non-technical but include links to our SOC 2 report + DPA.
- Neha: short 2-slide exec pack (2–3 bullets) for the Lydia intro — include projected 12-mo $ savings and a single-line ask (intro + budget band). Use the ROI model attached in the thread as source.
- Jonas: quick pricing bands (pilot vs committed) and a one-line on cancellation/terms we can send to procurement.

Also drafting a 3-bullet talk track for Priya to use with Lydia (feel free to iterate):
- We can reduce per-message LLM costs by ~40% within 90 days by moving to Dedicated inference and workload-aware batching.
- Maintain production SLAs with automatic fallbacks to hosted variants; we handle model rollouts and can pin versions for stability.
- Minimal engineering lift: Redwood provides deployment templates and a customer success plan for onboarding.

I’ll attach the ROI model and SOW to the workshop calendar invite once we lock the slot.

Thanks — Marissa
